name: Emma Davis
life: “I still remember a pensioner posing proudly in a mended cardigan.” On Tuesday, near the brick passage off the shop row, Emma takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I live across the landing. I asked for free sittings for the old people nobody photographs unless they're blowing candles out.
appearance: Emma is easy to recognize by two white streaks in otherwise dark hair and a small notch in the left eyebrow. Usually dressed in a brown corduroy jacket with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair, Emma gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in when listening.
personality: Emma gets protective of anybody who comes into a meeting unprepared. Emma privately wishes people would notice the amount of preparation behind this apparent ease.
agenda: To secure portrait sittings for overlooked neighbors.
family: Vera Rios is Emma’s second cousin. Emma sets the time to leave. Vera picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The small signature*, Vera says, “For years I bought my crews soup from that cart.”
connections: Ingrid Kaur. A free sitting for a pensioner and an after-school session share the same sink.

reactions.response: Emma asks the person crying whether they want to go somewhere quieter, leaving them control over the next step.
